input: Write a due diligence memo on Canva

team.claim: Founders and current executive leadership: Melanie Perkins (CEO & co-founder), Cameron Adams (CPO & co-founder), Cliff Obrecht (COO & co-founder), Zach Kitschke (CMO), Jennie Rogerson (Global Head of People); HQ Sydney, Australia.

Current executive roster (aggregator): Kelly Steckelberg (CFO), Todd Carpenter (Chief Legal Officer & Corporate Development), Rob Giglio (Chief Customer Officer), Nirmal Govind (Chief Algorithms Officer), Guy Kawasaki (Chief Evangelist).

CFO Damien Singh, with the company since 2016, resigned in February 2024 after the company launched an internal investigation into allegations of inappropriate behaviour, with no successor named at the time.
Five executives with backgrounds at Meta, Adobe and Google departed over the 18 months to August 2024, concentrated in divisions responsible for selling to large corporate customers.
Canva laid off 10 technical writers in late March 2025, the company's first known redundancy round, nine months after co-founders directed staff to use AI tools wherever possible.
Four senior leaders left in May 2026, including growth lead Iain Dowling (resignation announced 18 May 2026 after eight years) and senior engineering director Jonathan Ross (leaving end of May 2026).
Long-serving chief technology officer Brendan Humphreys stepped down earlier in 2026 after 12 years in the role.
Head of product Robert Kawalsky; Head of Europe is Duncan Clark (co-founder of acquired Flourish).
Anwar Haneef is GM and Head of Ecosystem at Canva.

output.company: Canva (Canva Pty Ltd and related entities; Sydney, Australia)

funding.claim: Series F, September 2021: US$200M led by T. Rowe Price with Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer Venture Partners, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree, at a US$40B valuation.

Funding history (aggregator): Series A Oct 2015 $15M at $165M; Series B Sep 2016 $15M at $349M; Series C Jan 2018 $40M at $1B; Series D May 2019 $70M at $2.5B; D ext. Oct 2019 $85M at $3.2B and Jun 2020 $60M at $6B; Series E Apr 2021 $71M at $15B; total raised $587.49M across 19 rounds; secondary price data from Clarity and Forge.

Secondary sales: US$1.58B in April 2024 at a US$26B valuation, another at US$32B (Oct 31, 2024), and an August 2025 employee secondary at US$42B; over US$2.5B of liquidity provided to investors since 2023 (company claim).

Investor markdowns of the $42B valuation (per US regulatory filings, June 2026 quarter): T. Rowe Price to implied US$38.2B (-9.1%), Franklin Templeton to US$39.3B (-6.3%), Blackbird -17% to US$34.9B; independent valuer set the staff share price at ~US$31B.
Secondary-market implied valuation ~$37.03B as of 2026-11-09, down 11.84% (aggregator data); early investors reportedly cut valuation to ~$35B earlier in 2026.

IPO: hiring US staff to rehearse earnings calls and manage sell-side analysts; Cliff Obrecht said in April 2026 the company was 'fully IPO ready' and assumed a 2027 listing, but timing uncertainty has grown amid AI costs and product delays; spokesperson says nothing new to share on IPO.

output.verdict: Canva looks strong on scale and durability: 265M+ monthly users, 31M paid subscribers, ~$4B ARR, historically profitable with ~A$1B in cash, 95% Fortune 500 penetration and a flagship OpenAI partnership. A closer look is needed on the 2026 inflection: ballooning AI costs that cut the growth forecast from 30% to 20% and triggered the first-ever 22% layoff, investor markdowns of the $42B valuation toward ~$35B, senior turnover (CFO resignation amid an internal investigation, CTO departure, four senior leaders in May 2026), and ASIC penalties for chronically late financial reporting ahead of a now-uncertain IPO.

business.claim: Canva, launched in 2013, is an online design and publishing tool with a mission to 'empower everyone in the world to design anything and publish anywhere'; it also operates the Affinity creative suite.

Sells freemium/SaaS digital design tools (Docs, Sheets, Whiteboards, Presentations, photo/video editors, websites, PDF editor, print) under paid tiers Canva Pro, Canva Business, Canva Enterprise, plus Education and Nonprofits plans.

AI product suite Canva AI (Magic Write, Magic Layers, Canva Code, Magic Resize, Magic Animate, Translate, Magic Insights, Magic Formulas); in 2025 it launched a 'Creative Operating System' and the Canva Design Model, described as 'the world's first design-aware AI'.
Targets enterprise, small business, agencies, education, government, healthcare, retail and nonprofits across industries; company claims 95% of the Fortune 500 use Canva.
Operates in 190 countries with 100+ languages; campus hubs in the UK, US, Australia, Philippines, New Zealand, Czech Republic, Austria and China; staff in 37 countries.

Growth by acquisition: Leonardo.Ai (July 2024, reported ~$80-320M), Affinity (2024), MagicBrief (January 2025), Cavalry and MangoAI (February 2026), plus Flourish (2021) and seven European acquisitions.

Freemium model where paying users subsidise free users; from FY2025 the group consolidates through Canva Australia Holdings Pty Ltd, and in 2026 it is shifting part of the commercial model from subscription to AI credits ('Canva 2.0').

traction.claim: Company claim: 220M+ monthly active users and 30B+ designs created.
Company claim: 265M+ monthly active users, 31M+ paid users, and $4B ARR by end of 2025, with ~20% MAU growth.
Company claim: 95% of the Fortune 500 use Canva.
Named customers (company claim): Zoom, Bloomingdale's, Danone, Airbnb, Salesforce, HubSpot, Expedia Group, Keller Williams, Aramark and Kellanova.

Company claim (COO Cliff Obrecht): B2B business (companies with 25+ seats) grew 100% to $500M ARR; majority of revenue from North America; lower-priced subscriptions launched in Pakistan, Uruguay, Morocco and Jamaica.
Partnership: first design deep-research connector and MCP Server for OpenAI's ChatGPT, plus one-click integration with Salesforce Agentforce; Canva GPT usage up 375% YoY (company claim).
Named one of the 'Magnificent Seven' pilot partners for OpenAI's Apps in ChatGPT at OpenAI Developer Day; 26M+ conversations with the Canva app on ChatGPT by October 2025 (company claim).
Company claim: 100 million teachers, students and education leaders use Canva monthly in 190+ countries; acquired MagicBrief in 2025; launched the new Affinity app free for everyone.

red_flags.claim: Layoff of 1,271 people (22% of staff) announced November 2026 - growth slowed for the first time in a decade, per CEO Melanie Perkins.

Valuation markdowns from $42B: T. Rowe Price -9.1% to US$38.2B, Franklin Templeton -6.3% to US$39.3B, Blackbird -17% to US$34.9B; internal staff share price set at ~US$31B; early investors cited at ~$35B - a large gap to the last official $42B figure.
Revenue growth forecast cut from 30% to 20% for 2026 amid rising AI costs, with delays to key product rollouts told to investors in July 2026.

Reports say the Nasdaq float once expected in 2027 has been shelved with no firm timing; patience is fraying among employees and earliest investors over realising value of holdings; Blackbird (~10% holder) is weighing shifting part of its stake into continuation funds.

CFO Damien Singh resigned in February 2024 amid an internal investigation into allegations of inappropriate behaviour, and the company's transparency over it was criticised; five big-tech-hired executives in enterprise-sales divisions left within the following 18 months.
ASIC infringement notices of A$792,000 for financial reports lodged years late across four entities, flagged as a reputational/underwriter scrutiny risk ahead of any IPO.
2019 data breach affecting data of 139 million users, including encrypted passwords and some Google tokens.

Competitive threat from AI startups (e.g., Gamma) and general-purpose chatbots (ChatGPT, Gemini); Apple launched a $12.99/month Creator Studio bundle; LLM referral traffic is rising but AI costs per user have jumped ('from cents per month to many, many more cents' per COO Obrecht).

reputation.claim: Glassdoor (aggregator): 3.8/5 across 922 reviews; 71% would recommend to a friend; 86% CEO approval for Melanie Perkins; senior management 3.1, career opportunities 3.4, work/life balance 3.6; lower ratings from women (3.0 vs 4.2 for men).

Recent Glassdoor reviews (aggregator) describe a 'cult like culture', insecure leaders, favoritism and people 'disappearing' with little explanation (May 2026, 3.0); inconsistent decision-making and bureaucracy (Jan 2026, 2.0); disorganized sales ops and staff let go without performance improvement plans (Jul 2025, 2.0).
Blind (aggregator): 3.8/5 across 485 reviews, with a recent review titled 'Nepotistic and Psychologically Unsafe'.

An anonymous verified Blind post (April 2026) from a 4-year staffer alleged top-down 'founder-mode' operating with decision-making collapsed into a small inner circle and strong people leaving or disengaging; investor Jason Lemkin (SaaStr) said his 8-year Canva usage drifted to nothing and values the company at ~US$12B.
Pricing changes in 2024 prompted customer backlash, to which Canva publicly responded.
Company transparency was criticised over the CFO's February 2024 resignation: the facts only emerged days later after questions from the Australian Financial Review and others.
May 2026 senior departures came amid broader staff concerns about job security as Canva repositions as an AI platform.

missing_fields: sanctions exposure: no sanctions or export-control actions against Canva found in the sources reviewed
current CFO appointment date for Kelly Steckelberg confirmed only via an aggregator org chart (theorg.com)

financial_signals.claim: Filed accounts: revenue US$2.1B for calendar 2024 (up from US$1.44B in 2023 and US$962M in 2022); net loss US$242M in 2024 and combined 2022-24 losses of US$692M; operating cash flow US$263M in 2024; ~A$1B cash at end of 2024.
Company claim: $4B ARR by end of 2025, up 35% YoY per COO Cliff Obrecht (Web Summit Qatar, Feb 2026); the company's 2025 wrap separately states revenue reached $3.5B in 2025.
Sacra estimate (third-party): $4B ARR at end of 2025, up 43% YoY from $2.8B in 2024; 265M MAU, 31M paid subscribers.

Headcount trend: 2,000+ (2021) to ~4,000 (Feb 2024) to ~5,000 (Oct 2024, ~1,000 hired in a year) to ~5,500 (Aug 2026); cut the cost of running AI by ~90% and built a 140-person in-house AI research arm.

Laying off 1,271 people (22% of staff) amid a growth slowdown; revenue growth forecast cut to 20% from 30% due to ballooning AI costs; growth slowed for the first time in a decade, with CEO Melanie Perkins calling it 'our hardest year yet' (company claim).

Restructuring affects 1,271 people losing jobs, relocating or changing roles; staff in 37 countries; Sydney to become the primary home for more product teams with hybrid workers in office 2-3 days a week from next year.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: ASIC fined four Canva entities (Canva Pty Ltd, Canva Operations, Canva Trading, Fusion Books) A$792,000 total (A$198,000 each in infringement notices) for late lodgement of FY24 financial reports; the FY24 consolidated report was lodged 27 March 2026, almost 11 months late, and 2023 accounts were more than two years late; ASIC made financial reporting misconduct a 2026 enforcement priority.

Canva and US music-rights firm Crunch Digital are suing each other in the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles: Canva alleges Crunch improperly disclosed confidential music-usage data to third-party royalty platform Pathfinder Royalties; Crunch alleges it was pushed out after raising 'potential licensing issues affecting Canva's operations' and seeking extra payment for scope expansion.

Canva did not notify the Australian Competition & Consumer Commission (ACCC) of its Leonardo.AI acquisition; the ACCC contacted Canva and its legal advisers attended an online meeting with antitrust officials, per documents obtained by MLex under freedom-of-information laws.

May 2019 data breach: hacker 'Gnosticplayers' claimed theft of data on 139 million users, including usernames, email addresses, real names, city/country and encrypted passwords, with some Google tokens stolen; Canva contacted the FBI and engaged a forensics team; its breezy customer notification email was criticised.

A former marketing manager's family medical records, financial records and ID documents stored on a personal Canva Pro account were exposed after account access changes in July 2026, prompting a NSW District Court interim injunction (Nehme v The Art Scene); Canva is a party of interest, not a defendant, and did not respond to the masthead's request for comment.
